findings.how: Mid-session refusal (round 1, 7b1b2cb): an authentication error or 401 in a conversation or task makes the host call getAuthStatus(). If the sign-in no longer holds, the phase becomes error/sign-in: the handle says 'Sign-in refused', settings show Sign in and Check again, and the bubble gets Open settings. Expiring GitHub App tokens (round 2, 9a3a788): pollDeviceGrant keeps access_token, refresh_token, expires_in and refresh_token_expires_in, plus the issuing client id. TokenStore stores the grant as JSON, a token alone in the old format, and still reads old files. GrantKeeper renews the grant an hour before it expires with GitHub's refresh_token grant, which needs no client secret for a device-flow token. GitHub's docs (docs.github.com/en/apps/creating-github-apps/authenticating-with-a-github-app/refreshing-user-access-tokens, fetched 2026-10-28) say client_secret is 'Required unless the user access token was generated using the device flow'. So the verifier's 'needs the client secret' does not hold for Ember. The keeper saves the renewed grant and reconnects Copilot once AgentHost.idle is true (no start, answer, queued request or task), or two minutes before the old token ends. If GitHub can't be reached it retries a minute later. If GitHub refuses, it stops, and the round 1 sign-in error then appears. A stored grant that ran out while Ember was off is renewed before it is used (freshen, at most once a minute). Sign out stops renewal. With 'Expire user authorization tokens' off, nothing changes. Either app setting therefore works. The owner's choice of setting and the first real long session are still worth a release-checklist line (see ciOnly).

ciOnly: The GitHub App Iv23liXa8A1wDXYg2jYw must have 'Enable Device Flow' on. The planned ci.yml step POSTs https://github.com/login/device/code with client_id=Iv23liXa8A1wDXYg2jYw and expects a device_code. This container's proxy blocks that endpoint.
That Copilot accepts this app's ghu_ user tokens, and whether the app needs a Copilot-related account permission for that: only a first real sign-in on a machine with a Copilot account can prove it.

Token renewal against real GitHub: the request shape (client_id, grant_type=refresh_token, refresh_token, no client_secret, as GitHub's docs allow for device-flow tokens) is unit-tested with a fake GitHub. A real renewal happens only after about 7 h of a real session, so it should be on the release checklist. The owner can instead turn 'Expire user authorization tokens' off for the app; then Ember stores a token without expiry and renews nothing. Either setting works with this branch.

The Windows and macOS wording of the GitHub CLI install steps (winget, brew), and the doctor row on those OSes, are unit-tested with fakes only. Real Windows/macOS CI or a manual run shows the rendered window (only builds without a client id show it).
safeStorage keeping the larger JSON grant under Windows DPAPI and the macOS Keychain: TokenStore is unit-tested with a fake box only.
final.notes:
On the relayed user request ("Have you resumed?"): yes. This run picked up the package's second round. An earlier, stopped run of this step had already committed six round-two commits (83ef321..9a3a788). I reviewed each of them, kept them, re-checked that their tests fail without the fix, and added two commits (3719b80, d6100ef).

Lead to confirm before merging (#93): the relayed user request in this run says nothing about the client id. The id Iv23liXa8A1wDXYg2jYw comes from common.md's S1 Update and lead-notes.md ('from the user, 2026-10-27 ~06:05'). It is public by design and sits alone in cdce845, so it can be reverted without touching anything else if the user did not send it.

#138: the verifier said refresh needs the client secret. GitHub's own docs say client_secret is 'Required unless the user access token was generated using the device flow' (docs.github.com/en/apps/creating-github-apps/authenticating-with-a-github-app/refreshing-user-access-tokens, fetched 2026-10-28). So the refresh was implemented, and Ember works with 'Expire user authorization tokens' on or off.

One edge case is left on purpose. If renewal before use (freshen) succeeds but the keyring-backed write then fails (full or read-only disk), the old refresh token is already used up. The user then has to sign in again, which is the same outcome as before this change.

#147 is marked partial only because its doc line lives in the docs package's file (forDocs has the exact text). Scratch backups made for the fails-first checks were deleted.

docs/DEVELOPING.md §Connecting Copilot: the client id lives in app/main/agent/github-app.ts (GITHUB_CLIENT_ID, one line; EMBER_GITHUB_CLIENT_ID overrides it at run time). Without it the button reads 'Connect with GitHub CLI'. Install gh per OS: RHEL 8 `sudo dnf config-manager --add-repo https://cli.github.com/packages/rpm/gh-cli.repo` then `sudo dnf install gh`; Windows `winget install --id GitHub.cli`; macOS `brew install gh`. Ember asks gh for github.com's token (`--hostname github.com`). A token Copilot refuses gives way to the next source, and Check again passes over it.

PLAN.md §7 Q1 (registering Ember's GitHub App): register it with 'Expire user authorization tokens' turned off. Ember can't refresh expiring ghu_ tokens because GitHub's refresh grant needs the client secret. If it is left on, users must sign in again every 8 hours; Ember now shows 'Sign-in refused' and Sign in again when that happens (review #138).
README (docs package): optionally point each install section to the new 'Sign in to Copilot' section, which this package wrote.

CHANGELOG lines:
- Sign-in now says it needs a GitHub account with Copilot and the GitHub CLI, says how to install gh on this computer, and offers an Open cli.github.com button.
- A token Copilot refuses no longer hides a working gh sign-in, and a refused GITHUB_TOKEN or GH_TOKEN is named.
- The device-flow sign-in keeps waiting through network blips.
- A full or read-only disk no longer throws away a finished sign-in, and file errors name the file instead of saying 'reinstall'.
- GitHub 5xx, rate limits and timeouts while connecting are retried and said plainly.
- A sign-in refused mid-session shows 'Sign-in refused' with Sign in and Check again.
- Copilot errors no longer show raw text.
- 'Show me' guides no longer wait behind running tasks.
- Finished task sessions are deleted at once.
- Default models avoid premium ones, and costly models are marked in settings.
- With commands off, Ember points to Settings › Commands.
ciOnly: Windows: a winget-installed gh (Program Files\GitHub CLI\gh.exe) is found by ghCliPath, so ghInstalled() is true. `gh auth token --hostname github.com` runs hidden (windowsHide) and returns the github.com token. 'Connect with GitHub CLI' then connects within a few seconds of `gh auth login` in a new terminal. Without gh, 'Open cli.github.com' opens the browser.
macOS: from a Finder launch, Homebrew's gh in /opt/homebrew/bin is found and the same flow works. The token file's temporary-file-then-rename write works with the Keychain-sealed blob on APFS.
Windows: renameSync of github-token.bin.<pid>.tmp over an existing github-token.bin succeeds (MoveFileEx replace), including with Defender scanning.

Real Copilot runtime: what a revoked or expired token produces mid-session. The code assumes a session.error with errorType 'authentication' or statusCode 401, then getAuthStatus() answering isAuthenticated:false. The exact 5xx/429/timeout wording from models.list, and whether 'Timeout waiting for CLI server to start' is what a slow first launch throws.
Real Copilot listModels: billing.multiplier is present and meaningful, and the default picks are sensible. Only then is '(N× premium requests)' in the settings lists correct.

Device flow against github.com once the client id is in: polling survives a Wi-Fi or VPN drop and a proxy 502. Whether the registered app hands out expiring ghu_ tokens. Ember doesn't refresh them, so register with 'Expire user authorization tokens' turned off.
The rpm repository steps (dnf config-manager --add-repo https://cli.github.com/packages/rpm/gh-cli.repo, then dnf install gh) on a clean RHEL 8.4 with dnf-plugins-core.

verifierProblems.what: A SessionToolsTimeoutError is still not treated as passing. The report says TRANSIENT's 'timeout' covers it, but the error's message is "Copilot didn't report its session tools within 10 s." (session-config.ts:56): no 'timeout' or 'timed out'. I ran the reviewer's repro (release-review/rev-agent/startErr.ts) against the fix branch. That message still gives reason 'other' and is shown as it is. doStart retries only offline or 'not-answering', so a conductor whose verifySessionTools times out (conductor.ts:485) during a start is never retried. The reviewer's fix named SessionToolsTimeoutError explicitly. The 5xx, 429, 'timed out' and 'Timeout waiting for CLI server to start' cases are fixed and tested.
verifierProblems.fix: In startErrorReason and explainStartError, treat `err instanceof SessionToolsTimeoutError` (import it from ./session-config), or /didn't report its session tools/, as 'not-answering' / TRANSIENT_DETAIL. Add a case to host.test.ts 'a passing problem while connecting' where the start fails with that error: it should be retried after about 15 s and reach ready.

verifierProblems.what: The refresh-token part is left undone, and it now matters. The fix agent marked #138 partial: the mid-session refusal is handled and tested, and I verified it. Expiring GitHub App user tokens are not handled. With the client id now supplied (a GitHub App id, Iv23li…), this applies to release builds. GitHub Apps expire user tokens after 8 h unless the owner turns that off. pollDeviceFlow returns only access_token (it drops refresh_token and expires_in). With the default app setting, every device-flow user would get 'Sign-in refused' about every 8 hours.
verifierProblems.fix: Before release, the lead and owner confirm that 'Expire user authorization tokens' is off for app Iv23liXa8A1wDXYg2jYw. Put it on the release checklist next to the planned CI device-code check. If it must stay on: implement refresh (GitHub's refresh grant needs the client secret), or at least keep expires_in and ask the user to sign in again before it runs out.

verifierProblems.what: A behaviour change beyond the finding. refusedTokens lasts for the whole run and Sign out doesn't clear it. Scenario: the user's gh token was refused (the account had no Copilot). They get a seat, press Sign out, then 'Connect with GitHub CLI'. findToken skips the refused gh token every 3 s, and after 10 minutes the user is told 'Ember didn't see a new GitHub sign-in'. Before the fix, after Sign out (currentToken = null), the same press connected at once. Check again still works, because it falls back to a refused token.
verifierProblems.fix: Clear refusedTokens in the IPC.signOut handler (main.ts, next to `currentToken = null`). Or let the GitHub CLI wait loop fall back to a refused token, as Check again does, when nothing else is found.
